newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - May 27.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Roche Holding Ltd has agreed to acquire Corange, the parent company of Boehringer Mannheim, for $11 billion.
* Leading industrial nations have agreed to outlaw bribery as a way for companies to win commercial contracts.
* U.S. banks tightened their lending standards for consumers in the past three months, while loosening standards for some commercial borrowers.
* A survey by the Manpower temporary employment agency has found that the employment outlook for the third quarter is the strongest since 1988.
* A record libel judgement issued recently against Dow Jones & Co Inc's Wall Street Journal has been sharply reduced by a federal judge.
* "The Lost World: Jurassic Park," a film made by Seagram Co Ltd's Universal, brought in a record $90.1 million over the holiday weekend.
* General Motors Corp and the United Auto Workers union have reached a tentative agreement to end a strike at the automaker's Oklahoma City plant.
* The shakeup at Westinghouse Electric Corp's CBS has the network's affiliates bracing for more changes.
* News Corp Ltd has a tentative deal to join PrimeStar Partners, the satellite-dish TV venture owned by a bevy of cable operators.
* International Family Entertainment Inc, the parent company of the Family Channel, has held talks with Walt Disney Co.
* PepsiCo agreed to sell its PFS food-distribution subsidiary to AmeriServe Food Distribution Inc, a subsidiary of Holberg Industries Inc.
* PepsiCo has applied for the voluntary liquidation of South African bottler New Age Beverages.
* Price Communications has a definitive agreement to acquire Palmer Wireless Inc for $506 million, plus $380 million in debt assumption.

* Heard on the Street: Bridge loans, anyone? Investors gaily buying all of those new shares and junk bonds may not know it, but they are bailing Wall Street out of some potentially risky temporary loans, made in the frenzied competition by banks and brokerage firms to win underwriting business.

* Credit Markets: Hey buddy, can you spare a bond? As the federal budget deficit drops and new corporate debt shrinks, a dwindling supply of new bonds is aiding the bond market, and could help keep interest rates lower in the years ahead.
